title: North Sea Empire
capsule: The North Sea Empire (1013/1016–1042) was the personal union of England, Denmark, and Norway assembled by Cnut the Great (Knútr inn ríki), who conquered England in 1016 after his father Sweyn Forkbeard's brief conquest in 1013, became king of Denmark on his brother Harald's death in 1019, and annexed Norway in 1028 after expelling Olaf Haraldsson. At its height it was the dominant power of the northern seas, sometimes described as a thalassocracy, with tributary acknowledgment from Scottish kings and coastal Baltic rulers. Norway broke away before Cnut's death in 1035, and after the brief reunion of England and Denmark under Harthacnut (1040–1042), Harthacnut's sudden death ended the empire; Edward the Confessor restored Anglo-Saxon rule in England.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The component kingdoms' borders are tolerably well documented from saga tradition and Anglo-Saxon Chronicle sources; the precise extent of Norwegian and Scottish tributary relationships is uncertain, and the empire should be understood as a personal union rather than a unified territorial state.
